rad.io

Paste or drop any code or text. Every character becomes part of the music.

Click anywhere in the code to choose where playback starts, or to jump there while it plays.

Drop a file onto the code area to load it
How characters map to sound
CharacterSound
Letters, _ $Lead melody (a sampled grand piano by default, with notes that ring on into the next one; there's a synth lead option too). Common letters move the melody by small steps, rare letters make bigger leaps. Doubled letters repeat the note, and the previous/current pair picks the note length. Capitals are accented.
DigitsPlucked note at that scale degree (0–9).
=Kick drum
+ - * / %Hi-hat
< > ! & | ^ ~Snare
( [ {Pad chord that moves with nesting depth; the melody also climbs higher the deeper you are.
) ] }Soft resolution chord on the tonic.
" ' ` ; ?Bell tones.
Space, , . :Rest. Tabs mid-line are a longer rest.
NewlineA short rest, snapped to the next 8th note. Blank lines add no extra pause.
Chillstep styleAbout 70 BPM with the melody stretched out and thinned to a few long notes on a steady rhythmic grid that lines up with the drums. Each line is a section with its own pace (mostly slow, sometimes medium, occasionally lively) that opens on its chord root and stays near it, with quiet stepwise filler notes smoothing any leaps; the Melody pace menu (Busy / Medium / Relaxed) shifts all the paces together. A darker piano lead, soft piano chords, a recorded electric bass, and a big reverb (the chords and bass are real instruments because held low synth tones sound like a horn). The harmony follows a steady i–VI–III–VII loop with one change per new line, the bass and chord always change together, and the melody glides to the nearest note of each new chord. The chords are voiced low and compact under the melody and move as little as possible between lines, and the bass restates the root every bar (the chord every second bar) so the harmony never drops out. A steady half-time drum groove plays underneath (kick on 1, snare on 3, swung hats) and the kick gently ducks the pad and bass so the drums stay present.
Lo-fi styleAbout 80 BPM, composed on the same layout as Chillstep (sparse melody on a grid, the i–VI–III–VII chord loop) and then played like a lo-fi beat. The chords get a 9th on top and are played as short stabs that follow a boom-bap kick (kick on 1 with a ghost kick and pickup, snare on 2 and 4 a touch late, swung hats). The bass plays short, round notes on the kick pattern. Timing and volumes are slightly loose. The piano and chords go through a gentle tape wobble, some saturation and a dark lowpass in a small room, with quiet vinyl crackle over the top.
Rock / Metal styleAbout 150 BPM in Phrygian. Each line is a riff section: palm-muted guitar chugs on straight 8ths, a gallop, a syncopated half-time rhythm, or a driving run. The riff keeps going across line breaks. Only one part speeds up at a time: some sections have the lead run up and down the scale in 8ths over a steady rhythm, and others end in a half-bar burst of 16th chugs and double kick while the lead rests. Common letters chug on the section's root note and rarer ones move up the scale, brackets add power chords, the bass is its own part (several bar shapes that rotate, walking notes that follow the words in the line, and a walk up into the next section's root), and the drums follow the riff with a crash and snare roll into each new section, plus accents from the code (`=` adds kicks, math operators add hats, comparisons add ghost snares). A lead guitar with vibrato plays over the other sections, mostly a note per beat or per 8th with stepwise pickup notes; each section centers on a different scale step so it keeps moving. Guitar and bass are real recorded samples through a distortion and speaker-style filter chain.
Chiptune styleAbout 140 BPM in a major scale, built on the default composition and played on simple console-style voices: a quarter-width pulse-wave lead, chords turned into fast arpeggios on a thin pulse wave (one note per 16th, up and back down the chord), and a triangle-wave bass that bounces between its root and the octave on every 8th note. The character-driven drum hits go quiet and a tight beat takes over (kick on 1 and 3 with an occasional pickup, noise snare on 2 and 4, straight 8th hats). Digits and quotes keep their blips and plinks. Everything is synthesized, so nothing downloads.
Ambient styleAbout 60 BPM, built on the Chillstep layout (the same slow, sparse melody and i–VI–III–VII chord loop with one change per new line) but with nothing struck. Each chord change becomes one long, soft drone that lasts until the next change, with a low root and fifth underneath; the melody is thinned to a note every few beats and the notes ring long; bell chimes still mark quotes and semicolons, and every few bars a soft gust of wind chimes (two to four high notes close together, usually falling, ringing together for seconds) drifts through. The voices are slow-fading and synthesized (detuned triangle chords through a dark filter and a slow chorus, a soft sine lead with a long echo, sine bass) in a very large reverb. There are no drums, and nothing downloads.
Synthwave styleAbout 100 BPM in Natural minor, built on the default composition and played like an 80s night-drive track. A bright, detuned saw lead with a dotted echo and chorus plays the melody over a wide detuned saw pad (chords are held at least a beat and a half), the bass is a relentless 16th-note filtered saw on each line's root with the beats accented, and the character-driven drum hits give way to a steady four-on-the-floor beat (kick on every beat, snare on 2 and 4, offbeat hats with quiet 16th ghosts). Digits and quotes keep their blips and plinks. Everything is synthesized, so nothing downloads.
Techno / House styleAbout 124 BPM in Dorian, built on the default composition and played like a club track. The bass is an offbeat pump (short filtered saw notes on the "and" of every beat, with an occasional 16th pickup) on each line's root; the chords become minor-7th stabs (3rd, 5th and 7th of the line's chord) in a syncopated house rhythm that alternates between two bars; the melody is thinned to at most an 8th note's density and played as short plucks with a dotted echo. The character-driven drum hits give way to a four-on-the-floor beat (kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4, open hats on the offbeats, 16th closed hats), and the kick ducks the bass and stabs on every beat for the pumping feel. Everything is synthesized, so nothing downloads.
Trance styleAbout 138 BPM in Natural minor, built on the default composition and played like an uplifting trance track. Each line's chord is held as a big detuned supersaw pad with a fast 16th-note pluck arpeggio over it (up the triad and into the octave, then back down); the bass rolls, three 16ths between every kick, on the line's root; the melody is thinned to a note every few beats, lengthened, and played by a supersaw lead with a long dotted echo. When a chord lasts two bars or more, its last half bar is a snare roll that builds in volume. The character-driven drum hits give way to a four-on-the-floor beat (kick on every beat, clap on 2 and 4, open hats on the offbeats), and the kick dips the pad, arpeggio and bass on every beat for the pump. Everything is synthesized, so nothing downloads.
Minimal viewThe button next to Play hides everything except the {rad.io} strip, which fills the page and turns into the equalizer while music plays. Moving the mouse (or tapping) fades in Play / Pause, Stop and a Full view button, and they fade out again after a couple of seconds. Esc goes back to the full view and Space plays or pauses. The equalizer runs in this view even if the Visualizer box is off.
Evolving harmonyEach line's text picks its own chord root and register; every fourth line returns to the tonic. The melody lands on a chord tone on each beat, the step size depends on the letter pair (not just the letter), word-ending notes are longer, word starts are accented, and each line swells in pitch and volume. Turn it off for the plain mapping.
Background trackCanon: the melody is echoed an octave up, a beat or a bar or two later, as a soft sine tone panned slightly right (just the melody, no bass, chords or drums). Alternating lines: odd lines play in the foreground while even lines play at the same time as a lower background voice, each on its own clock. The background cursor is blue.
IndentationSets the bass note played at the start of each line.
Sounds: Tone.js. Piano samples: Salamander Grand Piano by Alexander Holm (CC BY 3.0). Guitar and bass samples: tonejs-instruments (CC BY 3.0). Code box: CodeJar and Prism.
